questions.q: Which of these is NOT a button on an Ops Pulse row?
questions.e: Won and Lost are Sales Pulse deal buttons. Ops rows carry Create case, Handled - hide, Comment, Open in CRM, and on overdue cases Resolve and Snooze +3d.

questions.q: Where does a comment left through a pulse actually end up?
o: In a spreadsheet the automation keeps
Only in the next pulse email
As a CRM Note titled [Ops Pulse] or [Sales Pulse], attached to the record and its company
As a reply in the sales@ mailbox
questions.e: Comments are stored as CRM Notes with an [Ops Pulse] or [Sales Pulse] title prefix. The prefix is how the pulse reads them back and re-renders them under the item.

questions.q: What does pressing Handled - hide on an awaiting-reply row do?
o: Hides the thread until the customer mails again
Hides it permanently and resolves its auto-created case if that case is still New or Acknowledged
Deletes the email from the mailbox
Assigns the thread to a colleague
questions.e: Handled means handled - the thread is suppressed permanently. A deliberately parked case at In Progress or a Waiting status is left open, and a genuinely new request from the same sender still arrives as fresh mail.

questions.q: Which edition of the Sales Pulse carries the data-quality audit and a pipeline attachment?
questions.e: Monday's Sales Pulse adds the weekly data check: a line-by-line pipeline file attached, a per-stage reconciliation, and AI timing proposals with a one-tap Apply.
